verify-drift.sh (same base/head) reports: sweet16 DRIFT, petunia DRIFT,
groot@dualie DRIFT, groot@forge DRIFT, avina none, hermes none, groot@rk3588
N/A (excluded). sweet16/petunia/dualie/forge/avina match the
reachability-based expected set exactly. hermes is the one place the sets
differ on paper: consumers.sh names it a consumer of llm-agents, but its
derivation is byte-identical
(/nix/store/fvnhw3j8z88lwn3pzisvjvrw8rbhwsi3-nixos-system-...drv, both
revisions) - a proven, not assumed, true negative. See Root cause below.
Once that is accounted for, actual and expected are the same set.

### Root cause

hosts/hermes/llm-agents-overlay.nix does bind
agentPkgs = inputs.llm-agents.packages.${system} (this is the syntactic
edge consumers.sh follows to flag hermes), but the overlay only ever
publishes it as llm-agents = agentPkgs // { hermes-agent =
hermesAgentBase.overridePythonAttrs (...); }, and hermesAgentBase itself is
built with pkgs.callPackage ../../lib/hermes-agent/package.nix { ... } -
the vendored package, entirely independent of the llm-agents input's
content (per the vendoring decision recorded for the plugin-manifest
packaging regression). hosts/hermes/home.nix only ever reads
pkgs.llm-agents.hermes-agent (the overridden vendor derivation); nothing in
hermes' evaluated configuration reads any other attribute of agentPkgs.
Nix's laziness means the new llm-agents input's package set is bound but
never forced, so bumping llm-agents cannot change anything hermes actually
builds. This matches prior documented policy (lib/hermes-agent is vendored
ahead of upstream) and is confirmed empirically by the identical hermes
.drv hash across both revisions - not merely assumed from the overlay's
structure.
